goals: Mechanistic: attribute runoff-generation partitioning (surface runoff vs subsurface drainage) to elevation-driven snow/melt regime and soil texture
Validation: compare simulated runoff against USGS stream-gauge discharge

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM resolves per-point water partitioning, snow, and runoff components across a stratified sample of the basin's elevation/soil heterogeneity.

answerable: Per-column runoff-component partitioning (QOVER vs QDRAI) and its sensitivity to soil texture
Elevation control on snow accumulation/melt and melt-driven runoff timing, to the extent resolved by 12 km NLDAS orographic precip/temperature and simulated SWE

not_answerable.aspect: Validation of runoff against USGS stream gauges
not_answerable.why: Single-column ELM has no lateral routing; columns produce point runoff, not integrated basin streamflow comparable to a gauge

not_answerable.aspect: Sub-12 km terrain control on snow/runoff (individual ridges, headwater microclimate)
not_answerable.why: NLDAS-2 nearest-cell forcing at ~12 km has no within-cell lapse rate; ridgetop SWE underestimated

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation band x dominant soil class), rule-based; NOT the user's 3 raw points
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands x ~2 dominant SSURGO soil classes per band = ~6, plus +2 replication in the rain-snow transition (highest runoff-generation sensitivity) and +2 to cover a distinct soil where present; smallest sample that spans the two named drivers.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Oversample the rain-snow transition (700-1300 m) where melt-driven infiltration-excess/saturation runoff is most sensitive; place columns on the dominant soil of each band, favoring valley/riparian positions for saturation-runoff behavior and mid-slope for infiltration-excess.
sampling_strategy.replication: 2 extra columns in the rain-snow transition band across differing soils to separate soil vs elevation signal in the most sensitive zone.

sampling_plan.reason: Baseline low-elevation runoff where precip falls mostly as rain; anchors the no-snow end of the elevation gradient.
Isolates soil-texture effect on infiltration vs surface runoff at low elevation.
Core zone where melt timing controls runoff generation; primary mechanistic target.
Separates soil control from elevation/snow control within the most sensitive band.
Tests saturation-excess runoff where low-permeability soil limits infiltration during melt.
High-elevation snowpack-driven runoff; establishes the snowmelt-dominated end member (SWE from H2OSNO/QSNOMELT).
Soil-texture contrast at the snow-dominated end of the gradient.

validation_design.comparison: aggregated — requires routing/area-weighted aggregation of column runoff to a gauge's contributing area; NOT achievable with current single-column output
validation_design.metric: bias, NSE, monthly hydrograph correlation (once aggregation exists)
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on number of in-basin gauges and their contributing areas

validation_design.observation_source: SNOTEL (if present in/near basin) — analog if not co-located
validation_design.comparison: analog — peak-SWE process check at nearest station; not requested but supports the elevation/snow mechanism
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on SNOTEL coverage; not in provided observations

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline NLDAS-2 forcing, native SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start

requires_capabilities.capability: runoff routing / basin aggregation of column runoff
requires_capabilities.why: USGS gauges measure integrated streamflow; single columns give point runoff
NLDAS nearest-cell has no within-cell lapse; underestimates ridge SWE
requires_capabilities.blocks: full resolution of elevation/snow control in high-relief headwaters

requires_capabilities.why: runoff/drainage partitioning depends on slow soil-moisture/water-table states
expander must resolve dominant soil class and elevation band per point
process check on the snow mechanism

assumptions: User-supplied point (46.62, -119.90) is OUTSIDE the domain bbox and is dropped/flagged; the other two fall within the intended elevation bands and are absorbed into the stratified plan rather than used verbatim.
Dominant soil classes per elevation band exist and are separable in SSURGO within the Naches; exact classes resolved downstream.
Forcing period drawn from 1980-2018 NLDAS-2 (CONUS), covering wet/dry years for the sensitivity analysis.
Runoff generation is treated as per-column water partitioning, not integrated basin discharge.
open_questions: Which/how many USGS gauges lie in-basin and what are their contributing areas (needed to scope any future aggregation)?
Was the out-of-domain point (46.62, -119.90) a typo for an in-basin location the user wants retained?
Is a SNOTEL-based snow process check desired to substantiate the elevation/snow mechanism?
Preferred forcing years / wet-vs-dry contrast for runoff sensitivity?
